long_biography.plain_text:
The sale of Sports Division gave Sir Tom Hunter the means to turn philanthropy into a second operating discipline. He and his wife, Marion, created The Hunter Foundation, initially focusing on education and entrepreneurship. Hunter describes its money as risk capital: fund experiments, measure them, and ask government to scale approaches that work.

That model has supported programmes in Scotland and international poverty-reduction partnerships, while preserving his preference for entrepreneurial methods over passive grant-making. The foundation also backs leaders of growing businesses through retreats, mentoring and peer networks. Hunter received the Carnegie Medal of Philanthropy after building this approach around practical trials, external evaluation and public adoption.
